title_en: Shima Bei Village Committee of Yuecheng Town, Yueqing City, Zhejiang Province v. Zhejiang Shunyi Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. — dispute over a cooperative real estate development contract
ruling_gist_en: According to Articles 18 and 19 of the Organic Law of the Villagers Committees of the PRC, the villagers' meeting shall be convened by the villagers committee. For matters involving the interests of villagers and other matters involving villagers' interests that the villagers' meeting deems should be discussed and decided by the villagers' meeting, the villagers committee must submit them to the villagers' meeting for discussion and decision before implementation. Agreements concluded by the villagers committee with others after lawfully convening the villagers' meeting for discussion and decision shall be deemed lawful and valid.

full_text_en:
Village Committee of Shimaibei Village, Yuecheng Town, Yueqing City, Zhejiang Province v. Zhejiang Shunyi Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. — dispute over contract for cooperative development of real estate

Ruling Summary

Under Articles 18 and 19 of the Organic Law of the Villagers Committees of the People's Republic of China, the villagers’ meeting shall be convened by the villagers committee. With respect to matters concerning the interests of the villagers and other matters concerning the interests of the villagers that the villagers meeting deems necessary to be discussed and decided at a villagers meeting, the villagers committee must submit them to the villagers meeting for discussion and decision before handling. An agreement entered into by the villagers committee with another party after lawfully convening a villagers meeting to discuss and decide the matter shall be recognized as lawful and effective.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court
(2006) Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 59

Appellant (Plaintiff at first instance): Village Committee of Shimaibei Village, Yuecheng Town, Yueqing City, Zhejiang Province, domiciled at Shimaibei Village, Yuecheng Town, Yueqing City, Zhejiang Province.
Legal Representative: Li Longkang, Director of the Villagers Committee.
Agent ad litem: Chen Xu, lawyer at Beijing Long An Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Zhao Hongshi, lawyer at Beijing Long An Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at first instance): Zhejiang Shunyi Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., domiciled at Building 1, Lane 283, Wansong East Road, Anyang Town, Rui'an City, Zhejiang Province.
Legal Representative: Yu Heping, Chairman of the Board.
Agent ad litem: Liu Xinwen, lawyer at Beijing Guangzhu Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Xu Bo, lawyer at Beijing Guangzhu Law Firm.

The Appellant, the Village Committee of Shimaibei Village, Yuecheng Town, Yueqing City, Zhejiang Province (hereinafter referred to as the Village Committee), and the Respondent, Zhejiang Shunyi Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Shunyi Company), were involved in a dispute over a contract for cooperative development of real estate. The Higher People's Court of Zhejiang Province rendered a civil judgment on May 18, 2006, in (2005) Zhe Min Yi Chu Zi No. 7. The Village Committee, dissatisfied with the judgment, appealed to this Court. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law and held a hearing on November 8, 2006, for the trial of this case. The Village Committee's agents ad litem, Chen Xu and Zhao Hongshi, and Shunyi Company's legal representative, Yu Heping, and agent ad litem, Liu Xinwen, appeared in court. This case is now concluded.

The court of first instance found the following facts upon trial: In January 2003, over 700 mu of land collectively owned by the Village Committee was expropriated by the Yueqing Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources. The Yueqing Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources returned to the Village Committee 70 mu of reserved land-use quotas, including plot C-c41 (hereinafter referred to as Plot No. 7) in dispute, to be used for the Village Committee's development operations, establishment of enterprises, and villagers' housing. After the land was expropriated, the land-contracting households strongly demanded compensation of RMB 300,000 per mu. Therefore, after discussion at a villagers' representative meeting, the Village Committee decided to develop Plot No. 7 to address the compensation issue for the land-contracting households. The Village Committee negotiated with Rui'an Huitong Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Huitong Company) several times to develop the plot. After discussion at the Village Committee's villagers' representative meeting, the Village Committee and Huitong Company successively entered into three agreements on August 30, 2003, September 9, 2003, and October 16, 2003. The agreement of August 30, 2003, stated that the parties reached the following agreement concerning the listing-for-transfer of Plot No. 7 (approximately 12.27 mu, subject to the attached map): 1. The Village Committee's net proceeds from the land transfer shall be ensured at RMB 50 million, i.e., regardless of the price at which Huitong Company acquired the land, Huitong Company shall pay the Village Committee a net amount of RMB 50 million. Any rights and obligations arising from changes in policies or regulations concerning the plot or any other factors shall have nothing to do with the Village Committee. 2. If another company acquires the plot during the listing-for-transfer and the Village Committee's net land transfer proceeds are less than RMB 50 million, Huitong Company shall make up the shortfall; if the Village Committee's net land transfer proceeds exceed RMB 50 million, the excess shall be shared equally between the parties. 3. Upon execution of this agreement, Huitong Company shall pay the Village Committee a deposit of RMB 30 million (including RMB 7 million already received) before September 10, 2003, with any excess to be refunded or deficiency to be made up after the listing ends. Huitong Company undertakes to complete the transfer of the plot within approximately six months from the signing of this agreement. 4. This agreement is executed in two copies, each party holding one for evidence. The agreement of September 9, 2003, stated that the Village Committee undertakes to have lawful use rights over Plot No. 7, with an approximate area of 12.27 mu, and, through a resolution of the villagers' representative assembly, decided to cooperate with Huitong Company in the development.

For this purpose, the parties reached the following agreement on relevant matters: 1. The Village Committee shall provide the above-mentioned land use rights, and Huitong Company shall provide funds, technology, management, and operating resources, etc., primarily for development matters. The parties shall jointly develop the above land and then share the proceeds in an agreed proportion. 2. To demonstrate good faith in the cooperation, Huitong Company shall pay RMB 30 million as upfront funds to the Village Committee's account, to be used for expenses related to the preliminary cooperation, etc. 3. Huitong Company shall, from the date hereof, mobilize and organize personnel to conduct surveys, measurements, and designs of the land, complete relevant operating technical data and drawings, and carry out necessary planning and advertising to enhance the commercial value of the plot. 4. The detailed matters of cooperation shall be negotiated separately. Pending the conclusion of a detailed agreement, the parties' cooperation shall not cease. The agreement of October 16, 2003, stated that the Village Committee holds a piece of returned land that had been nationalized, with an approximate area of 12.27 mu, designated as Plot No. 7 in the planning scheme. The Village Committee undertakes to have lawful use rights over the plot. After convening multiple villagers' representative assembly meetings, the Village Committee decided to jointly develop the plot with Huitong Company. For this purpose, Huitong Company paid the Village Committee RMB 30 million and, at the same time, mobilized personnel to carry out consultation, design, survey, and planning work for the cooperative development, substantially completing all pre-development work, thereby significantly increasing the value of the plot.

The Village Committee now proposes that, as required by the Yueqing Municipal Land Administration Authority, the plot must be transferred through listing. Therefore, the parties' cooperation must be renegotiated. After a resolution of the villagers' representative assembly, the Village Committee reached the following new agreement with Huitong Company: 1. In order to continue the cooperation, Huitong Company shall participate in the bidding for the listing-for-transfer of the above plot conducted by the Yueqing Municipal Land Administration Authority. If Huitong Company acquires the ownership of the plot, considering Huitong Company's prior investment of human and financial resources that increased the land value, the parties agree: regardless of the amount of land transfer proceeds returned to the Village Committee by the Land Administration Authority after the listing, the Village Committee's net proceeds shall be RMB 50 million. Any excess amount shall be the profit share for Huitong Company's input and efforts during the previous cooperation, and this amount, together with the RMB 30 million already paid by Huitong Company to the Village Committee, shall be returned by the Village Committee to Huitong Company. The return shall be made within 7 days after the Village Committee receives the transfer proceeds from the Land Administration Authority; otherwise, a penalty of 0.1% per day shall be paid. At the same time, if Huitong Company is financially strained in paying the transfer proceeds to the Land Administration Authority, it may request the Village Committee to return the previously paid RMB 30 million in advance, and the Village Committee shall accommodate such request. 2. If another entity acquires the ownership of the plot through listing, the Village Committee shall return the RMB 30 million already invested and paid by Huitong Company. At the same time, if the land transfer proceeds returned to the Village Committee by the Yueqing Municipal Land Administration Authority exceed RMB 50 million, the excess portion shall be the proceeds of the parties' preliminary cooperation, to be shared equally. The Village Committee shall pay Huitong Company its half share, with the time for payment and penalty clauses consistent with Article 1. 3. Huitong Company unconditionally guarantees that, given its previous commitment that the total land price after design, planning, and cooperative development would reach RMB 50 million—which was a precondition for the Village Committee's consent to the cooperation—if the Land Administration Authority returns an amount less than RMB 50 million to the Village Committee, Huitong Company guarantees to make up the shortfall and fulfill its commitment. Otherwise, it shall bear liquidated damages of RMB 30 million. 4. All prior oral and written agreements between the parties shall be null and void, and this agreement shall prevail. 5. Regardless of the circumstances, the parties' agreement on the determination of the above amounts of interests shall be irrevocable. If any clause of this agreement becomes invalid for any reason, the relevant amounts shall be converted into compensation of the same amount.

After the agreement was signed, Huitong Company, in accordance with the parties' agreement, successively paid the Village Committee RMB 30 million and carried out preliminary design, survey, and fund-raising work for the development of the plot.

On November 27, 2003, Huitong Company changed its name to Shunyi Company.

On November 5, 2003, the Village Committee submitted a report to the Yueqing Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources, requesting that Plot No. 7 be listed for transfer. On January 22, 2004, the Yueqing Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources conducted a bidding for the use rights of Plot No. 7, and Shunyi Company won the bid at a price of RMB 156.5 million. On February 27, 2004, Shunyi Company entered into a State-owned Land Use Rights Transfer Contract with the Yueqing Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources. From March 8, 2004, to May 12, 2004, Shunyi Company paid the full land transfer price of RMB 156.5 million to the Yueqing Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources in five installments. In accordance with its agreement with Shunyi Company, the Village Committee transferred RMB 82.4 million to Shunyi Company.

On July 11, 2005, the Village Committee filed a lawsuit with the Higher People's Court of Zhejiang Province, seeking: a declaration that the agreement signed by the parties on October 16, 2003, was invalid, and an order for Shunyi Company to return RMB 52.4 million to the Village Committee; and that the litigation costs be borne by Shunyi Company. The facts and grounds were: In 2003, the Yueqing Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources expropriated 700 mu of land from the Village Committee and, as required, returned 70 mu as resettlement reserved land for the Village Committee, to be used for villagers' housing and commercial development. The Village Committee subsequently entered into two agreements with Shunyi Company on August 30, 2003, and October 16, 2003, concerning Plot No. 7 (12.27 mu of the reserved land). The general intent of the agreements was that, regardless of the amount of land transfer proceeds returned to the Village Committee by the land administration authority, the Village Committee would net RMB 50 million. If Shunyi Company won the bid, the excess amount together with the RMB 30 million deposit already paid by Shunyi Company to the Village Committee would be returned to Shunyi Company; if another entity won the bid, the excess would be shared equally between the parties. On January 22, 2004, the Yueqing Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources lawfully conducted a bidding for the use rights of Plot No. 7, and Shunyi Company won the bid at RMB 156.5 million. According to relevant regulations, the Yueqing municipal government returned RMB 122.4 million of the land transfer proceeds to the Village Committee. On April 21, 2004, and May 8, 2004, the Village Committee transferred a total of RMB 82.4 million to Shunyi Company in two installments (including the RMB 10 million deposit returned by the Village Committee to Shunyi Company).

The plaintiff claimed that the villagers were unaware of the above conduct at the time. Subsequently, the villagers demanded that the Village Committee recover from Shunyi Company RMB 52.4 million, representing the amount in excess of the RMB 30 million deposit already paid by Shunyi Company, but the Village Committee failed to perform its duties. The villagers also petitioned the government to cancel Shunyi Company's winning bid, which was not supported. The villagers then filed a lawsuit in court challenging the validity of the agreement and seeking a refund, but the case was not accepted due to standing issues. Accordingly, the villagers, in accordance with the Organic Law of the Villagers Committees of the People's Republic of China, re-elected new members of the Village Committee and a new director. After the new Village Committee was established, it requested the government to voluntarily annul the bid, but the government remained inactive. In the bidding, the starting price of the land was RMB 70 million, and Shunyi Company won at RMB 156.5 million, while the second bid was only RMB 200,000 lower than Shunyi Company's winning price. Therefore, the agreement entered into by the parties constituted malicious collusion that harmed the collective interests of the villagers and the lawful interests of other bidders, and thus was a void contract. Each party should return the property obtained from the other. Shunyi Company had paid the Village Committee a deposit of RMB 30 million, and the Village Committee made two payments totaling RMB 82.4 million to Shunyi Company. Therefore, Shunyi Company should return RMB 52.4 million to the Village Committee, being the amount in excess of the deposit already paid.

On July 11, 2005, Shunyi Company filed a counterclaim with the court of first instance, but later applied to withdraw it, which was granted by the court of first instance.

Shunyi Company argued in its defense: According to the unified land expropriation agreement signed by the Village Committee and the Yueqing Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources on January 28, 2003, and the documents Yue Zheng (1999) No. 7 and Yue Zheng (2000) No. 149 issued by the Yueqing municipal government, the acquisition of the subject matter of the parties' cooperative operation (the land) was lawful. The Village Committee convened a villagers' representative assembly on August 29, 2003, and lawfully adopted a valid resolution of the villagers' representatives. At that villagers' representative assembly, the number of persons to be present was 89, while 72 actually attended. The resolution was passed with 71 votes in favor and 1 abstention (among them, 44 villagers' representatives were expected to attend, 39 actually attended; 45 party members were expected to attend, 33 actually attended, and 5 party members were away). The cooperation between the parties was based on openness and voluntariness, and the Village Committee's claim of malicious collusion was untrue. The two agreements of August 30, 2003, and October 16, 2003, were signed after the villagers' representative assembly, and their basic content was consistent with the assembly's resolution. However, they further specified the operation mechanism when the land's listing price exceeded or fell below RMB 50 million, as well as the penalty clauses for breach. In essence, they defined the rights, obligations, and penalties of the parties. After the agreements were signed, because the government had not determined the floor area ratio for Plot No. 7, and the level of the floor area ratio determines the commercial value of the land, Shunyi Company did a substantial amount of work. On January 12, 2004, the Yueqing Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources issued a Construction Land Approval Letter, which provided for a floor area ratio of <5.8 and a building area of <50,610 square meters, thereby enhancing the commercial value of Plot No. 7. In addition, pursuant to the parties' agreement, Shunyi Company also carried out preliminary land planning, design, and survey work. On February 28, 2004, Shunyi Company won the use rights of Plot No. 7 at a price of RMB 156.5 million. At the same time, Shunyi Company entered into a State-owned Land Use Rights Transfer Contract with the Yueqing Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources, which was notarized. In summary, the agreement entered into by the parties represented their true intentions and complied with relevant laws and regulations. Therefore, the agreement was valid, and the parties should continue to perform it. Shunyi Company requested that the court reject the Village Committee's claims.

The court of first instance held that, considering the arguments of both parties, the focus of the dispute in this case was the validity of the agreement signed by the parties on October 16, 2003. The Village Committee claimed that the agreement was made by the previous village committee and party branch without the villagers' knowledge, violating the relevant provisions of the Organic Law of the Villagers Committees of the People's Republic of China; and that the agreement constituted malicious collusion between the parties, harming the lawful interests of the villagers' collective and other bidders, and should therefore be declared invalid according to law. Shunyi Company argued that the agreement had been discussed and adopted by the villagers' representative assembly, and there was no factual evidence of malicious collusion; after signing the agreement, Shunyi Company had done substantial work to develop the plot and had obtained the state-owned land use rights through lawful listing-for-transfer procedures; the agreement reflected the true intentions of the parties, complied with legal provisions, and was a valid agreement.

The court of first instance held that the records of the villagers' representative assembly meeting confirmed that the Village Committee, in accordance with the provisions of Article 19 of the Organic Law of the Villagers Committees of the People's Republic of China concerning the disposition of matters involving the interests of villagers, had submitted the matters covered by the parties' agreement to the villagers' representative assembly for discussion and adoption. The Village Committee's claim that the villagers were unaware of the matter was inconsistent with the facts and was not accepted. The document Le Tu Zi [2003] No. 76 from the Yueqing Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources only showed that on June 15, 2003, the Bureau sent a letter to the village committee and party branch of Shimaibei Village, Yuecheng Town, requesting them to terminate the planned public bidding for Plot No. 7 organized by the village committee and party branch, and did not prove the existence of malicious collusion between the parties. Although the starting price for the listing-for-transfer of the disputed plot was RMB 71 million and the final transaction price was RMB 156.5 million, both higher than the RMB 50 million agreed upon by the parties, there was no evidence to show that the parties engaged in malicious collusion before signing the agreement. The purpose of the parties in signing the agreement was to secure their respective interests, and the content of the agreement was discussed and adopted by the villagers' representative assembly; there was no issue of harming the collective interest. The Yueqing Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources had confirmed on February 27, 2004, that the listing-for-transfer of the use rights of the disputed state-owned land was concluded at RMB 156.5 million. The transferee, Shunyi Company, had already paid the full land transfer price of RMB 156.5 million and obtained the state-owned land use right certificate for the disputed plot on June 26, 2004. The entire listing process had been completed. Neither party disputed this, and the listing act was lawful and valid. Shunyi Company's participation in the listing did not violate the provisions on bidding, auction, and listing-for-transfer of state-owned land use rights, nor did it harm the interests of other bidders. This case did not involve the invalidating circumstance of malicious collusion harming the interests of the state, the collective, or a third party under Article 52(2) of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, nor any other invalidating circumstance under Article 52. Shunyi Company's argument that the agreement was valid was accepted. In accordance with Article 64(1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the court entered a judgment rejecting the Village Committee's claims. The court of first instance fixed the case acceptance fee at RMB 272,010 and the investigation fee at RMB 2,000, to be borne by the Village Committee.

The Village Committee, dissatisfied with the judgment of the court of first instance, appealed to this Court. It requested: 1. To set aside the judgment of the court of first instance; 2. To declare that the agreement signed by the parties on October 16, 2003, was invalid and order Shunyi Company to return RMB 52.4 million to the Village Committee; 3. The litigation costs to be borne by Shunyi Company. The main facts and grounds were: 1. Before the Village Committee signed the agreement with Shunyi Company, no villagers' meeting was convened; the "Record of Villagers' Meeting" was of unknown origin and should not be admitted as evidence; 2. Shunyi Company did not provide evidence to prove that it had increased the floor area ratio through its work; 3. The listing of the disputed land harmed the lawful interests of other bidders; 4. The signatures of villagers' representatives Zhang Congding, Tang Changmin, and Yang Mingzhong on the "Record of Villagers' Meeting" were forged and had no legal effect; 5. The three agreements were not discussed at a lawful villagers' representative assembly meeting; 6. The "Record of Villagers' Meeting" did not clearly specify how the portion exceeding RMB 50 million would be distributed.

Shunyi Company argued in its defense: Shunyi Company acquired the disputed land through lawful procedures; there was no illegal transfer relationship with the Village Committee, nor any malicious collusion with others; the obtaining of the "Record of Villagers' Meeting" was not contrary to law, and its authenticity could not be denied; the testimonies of the three villagers were contradictory and should not be admitted; the challenge to the validity of the listing was irrelevant to this case.

The facts found upon retrial by this Court were the same as those found by the court of first instance.

This Court held that the focus of the dispute in this case was: whether the agreement signed by the parties on October 16, 2003, was valid; how to deal with the proceeds of the land listing-for-transfer in the amount of RMB 122.4 million; and how to determine the challenge to the validity of the listing.

Regarding the issue of whether the agreement dated October 16, 2003, signed by both parties, is valid. The parties had entered into a total of three agreements. Prior to signing the August 30 agreement, the Village Committee convened a villagers' representative assembly on August 29, 2003, and adopted a meeting resolution. Its contents were: ensure a net land payment of RMB 50 million (any amount deducted by the land bidding department shall be borne by Shunyi Company and shall have no relation to the village), first pay a development deposit of RMB 30 million to solve difficulties and compensate the contracting households, and the remaining amount shall be paid in full (lump sum) after the listing; after the bidding price is determined, neither party shall renege. The next day, the parties signed an agreement stipulating that Shunyi Company shall ensure the Village Committee receives a net land transfer fee of RMB 50 million for the plot, i.e., regardless of the price at which Shunyi Company acquires the land, it shall pay the Village Committee a net amount of RMB 50 million. Any rights or obligations arising from changes in policies, regulations, or other factors related to the plot shall have no relation to the Village Committee. If another company acquires the plot through listing, and the net transfer fee received by the Village Committee is less than RMB 50 million, the shortfall shall be made up by Shunyi Company; if the net transfer fee received by the Village Committee exceeds RMB 50 million, the excess shall be split equally between the parties. On September 9 of the same year, the parties signed another agreement; as this agreement is unrelated to the disputed issue, it will not be repeated. On October 16, 2003, the parties signed a third agreement. In addition to stipulating that the Village Committee's net receipt shall be RMB 50 million, this agreement further explicitly provided that the portion exceeding RMB 50 million shall be the benefit share for Shunyi Company's input and efforts in the prior cooperation process, and this amount, together with the RMB 30 million already paid by Shunyi Company to the Village Committee, shall be returned by the Village Committee to Shunyi Company. The agreement also stipulated that all prior oral and written agreements between the parties before this agreement shall be null and void, and this agreement shall prevail.

Our court holds that the parties signed the August 30 agreement after the Village Committee convened the villagers' representative assembly. However, the Village Committee did not convene another villagers' representative assembly before the parties signed the October 16 agreement. Although the two agreements are substantially similar in terms of the amount of land transfer fee to be paid to the Village Committee and the handling of circumstances arising after the listing, the August 30 agreement did not explicitly provide that the portion exceeding RMB 50 million from the bidding would be fully returned by the Village Committee to Shunyi Company, nor did the villagers' representative assembly resolution contain such a provision. Therefore, as a new agreement, there is no evidence that the October 16 agreement was approved by the villagers' representative assembly. Shunyi Company's claim that the October 16 agreement was signed pursuant to a resolution of the villagers' representative assembly lacks sufficient factual basis; hence, this agreement should be held invalid. The first-instance judgment's finding that the October 16 agreement was valid is erroneous and should be corrected. The meeting minutes of the villagers' representative assembly provided by Shunyi Company can only prove that the August 30 agreement was signed after a resolution of the villagers' representative assembly. According to the Village Committee's meeting minutes, on August 29, 2003, the Village Committee convened a villagers' representative assembly, with 72 persons present, 71 signing in agreement with the meeting resolution, and 1 abstaining. In terms of the meeting procedure, it complied with the provisions of Article 18 of the Organic Law of the Villagers' Committees of the PRC. Furthermore, the content of the August 30 agreement was essentially consistent with the content of the villagers' representative assembly resolution, i.e., ensuring the Village Committee receives a net land payment of RMB 50 million, with no clear opinion on how to handle the portion exceeding RMB 50 million if Shunyi Company wins the bid. Therefore, the content of the agreement signed by both parties on August 30 was discussed and decided by the villagers' representative assembly, conforming to the provisions of Article 19 of the Organic Law of the Villagers' Committees of the PRC; hence, this agreement should be held valid. As for the issue raised during the trial by three villager representatives that the signatures on the villagers' representative assembly resolution were not their own, our court holds that even if some individual names on the meeting resolution were signed by others, this cannot thereby deny the meeting resolution adopted by the majority of villager representatives. Therefore, the Village Committee's claim that the August 30 agreement is invalid lacks evidence and is not supported.

Regarding the issue of how to handle the proceeds of RMB 122.4 million from the listing and transfer of Plot No. 7. Our court holds: According to the agreement, RMB 50 million of the RMB 122.4 million land price should belong to the Village Committee; the distribution of the remaining RMB 72.4 million between the parties is not explicitly stipulated. In distributing this sum, the interests of both parties should be balanced. Considering the specific circumstances of this case, Shunyi Company undertook some preliminary work on the land before the bidding, and this sum is related to the production and livelihood of the land-lost villagers. Since the circumstances of the two parties are not directly comparable, the amount to be distributed can be determined based on the principle of relative fairness, with each party receiving half, i.e., the Village Committee and Shunyi Company each receive RMB 36.2 million. Of the RMB 122.4 million land price, the Village Committee actually receives RMB 86.2 million; Shunyi Company actually receives RMB 36.2 million. Given that the Village Committee has already returned RMB 82.4 million to Shunyi Company, deducting the RMB 20 million deposit already paid by Shunyi Company but not yet refunded by the Village Committee, Shunyi Company shall pay an additional RMB 16.2 million to the Village Committee.

Regarding the issue of how to determine the objection to the validity of the listing. The Village Committee argued that the parties engaged in bid-rigging during the bidding, infringing upon the interests of a third party, and thus the listing should be invalid. Our court holds that after the Yueqing Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources confirmed the listing and transfer of the disputed land use rights, Shunyi Company won the bid, paid the full land transfer fee after winning, and has obtained the "State-owned Land Use Certificate" for the disputed plot. In this regard, if a third party raises an objection, asserting that the parties engaged in bid-rigging during the bidding, infringing upon its interests, such claim should be asserted by the third party to the relevant authorities, and the Village Committee has no right to assert it. The Village Committee's claim in this regard is not supported.

In summary, pursuant to the provisions of Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the judgment is as follows:

1. Set aside the civil judgment ( [2005] Zhe Min Yi Chu Zi No. 7) of the Zhejiang High People's Court;

2. Zhejiang Shunyi Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. shall, within fifteen days after this judgment takes effect, pay RMB 16.2 million to the Shimabei Village Committee, Yuecheng Town, Yueqing City, Zhejiang Province. In case of failure to perform the monetary payment obligation specified in this judgment within the prescribed period, interest on the debt for the period of delayed performance shall be doubled in accordance with the provisions of Article 232 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC;

3. Dismiss the other claims of the Shimabei Village Committee, Yuecheng Town, Yueqing City, Zhejiang Province.

The first and second instance case acceptance fees of RMB 544,020 and the investigation fee of RMB 2,000, totaling RMB 546,020, shall be borne equally by both parties, i.e., the Shimabei Village Committee, Yuecheng Town, Yueqing City, Zhejiang Province shall bear RMB 273,010, and Zhejiang Shunyi Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. shall bear RMB 273,010.

This judgment is final.
